definition: Flux is an open-source machine-learning software library and ecosystem written in Julia.
details: Its current stable release is v0.16.5 . It has a layer-stacking-based interface for simpler models, and has a strong support on interoperability with other Julia packages instead of a monolithic design. For example, GPU support is implemented transparently by CuArrays.jl. This is in contrast to some other machine learning frameworks which are implemented in other languages with Julia bindings, such as TensorFlow.jl (the unofficial wrapper, now deprecated), and thus are more limited by the functionality present in the underlying implementation, which is often in C or C++. Flux joined NumFOCUS as an affiliated project in December of 2021. Flux's focus on interoperability has enabled, for example, support for Neural Differential Equations, by fusing Flux.jl and DifferentialEquations.jl into DiffEqFlux.jl. Flux supports recurrent and convolutional networks. It is also capable of differentiable programming through its source-to-source automatic differentiation package, Zygote.jl. Julia is a popular language in machine-learning and Flux.jl is its most highly regarded machine-learning repository (Lux.jl is another more recent, that shares a lot of code with Flux.jl). A demonstration compiling Julia code to run in Google's tensor processing unit (TPU) received praise from Google Brain AI lead Jeff Dean. Flux has been used as a framework to build neural networks that work with homomorphic encrypted data without ever decrypting it. This kind of application is envisioned to be central for privacy to future API using machine-learning models. Flux.jl is an intermediate representation for running high level programs on CUDA hardware. It was the predecessor to CUDAnative.jl which is also a GPU programming language.

explainer.lead: Flux is an open-source machine-learning library and ecosystem written in Julia. It lets people build neural networks from layers while using other Julia packages for GPU computing, differential equations, and automatic differentiation.

tiers.eli5: Flux is like a box of building blocks for making learning programs in the Julia language. You can stack blocks to make a model, then borrow other Julia tools to do jobs such as running calculations on a graphics card. This means you do not have to find every tool inside one giant box.
tiers.practitioner: Simple Flux models use a layer-stacking interface, with support for convolutional and recurrent networks. Zygote.jl provides source-to-source automatic differentiation, while CuArrays.jl supplies transparent GPU support; DiffEqFlux.jl combines Flux with DifferentialEquations.jl for neural differential equations. Its package-based design differs from Julia wrappers around frameworks implemented in C or C++, which can be constrained by the underlying implementation.
tiers.paperLevel: Flux is an open-source Julia library and ecosystem for differentiable machine learning in which models are composed from layers and derivatives are obtained through Zygote.jl's source-to-source automatic differentiation. Its design emphasizes interoperability with independent Julia packages rather than a monolithic framework. It supports recurrent and convolutional networks and can be composed with DifferentialEquations.jl through DiffEqFlux.jl to express neural differential equations.

explainer.example: A small image classifier can be constructed by stacking convolutional layers in Flux. CuArrays.jl can provide GPU computation, and Zygote.jl can differentiate the model code to support gradient-based training.

usedIn.name: Neural differential equations
usedIn.detail: DiffEqFlux.jl combines Flux.jl and DifferentialEquations.jl to support models that join neural networks with differential equations.

usedIn.name: GPU-accelerated machine learning
usedIn.detail: CuArrays.jl implements GPU support transparently within Flux's Julia-based ecosystem.

usedIn.name: Privacy-preserving machine learning
usedIn.detail: Flux has been used to build neural networks that process homomorphically encrypted data without decrypting it.

explainer.inAi: Flux supports recurrent and convolutional networks and differentiable programming through Zygote.jl. It has also been applied to neural differential equations and neural networks operating on homomorphically encrypted data.
